scope: Source/evidence review of final ordinary unittest declaration/identity loader repair; no full G0, scanner, Lean, mathematical, hosted or federation acceptance claim

closed_findings.boundary: Custom TestCase constructors/metaclasses/attribute dispatch are refused before instantiation; declared function/code chains are captured before standard construction and compared afterward.
Default discovery enumerates actual ordinary-module dictionary declarations and does not invoke module __dir__ or __getattr__.
Named selector traversal checks the supported TestCase profile before class attribute access, uses raw static declaration inspection, and refuses non-module/non-class proxy/factory traversal.

Supported descriptors are exact built-in staticmethod/classmethod types; subclasses are refused. Constructor and dispatch-member inspection uses inspect.getattr_static, so the profile inspector does not invoke custom descriptors.

source_partition: Compared with c77ee122/50c0e2d first reviewed generation, IdentityLoader is the only changed existing top-level definition in either runtime. The actual function/code binding, body lifecycle, exception identity, synchronous None-return profile, accounting and classifier logic remain unchanged. Shared nine-definition identity blocks match by AST across both tools.
test_partition: Only the two existing identity methods for module population hooks and callable/constructor/descriptor factories expand; no identity-stage methods are deleted or added after the seven-method generation. All other methods retain exact AST identity.
preservation: All earlier AMEND reviews, failed omission probes, original failed normal run and generation-bound receipts remain intact. They are not overwritten or relabeled as final-source executions.
review_execution: Final review used source, AST, hashes and saved receipts only; no completed test or probe was rerun. Earlier new-counterexample executions remain explicitly generation-bound.
limitations: Trusted ordinary Python test source/runtime and source/runner custody are required; this is not an arbitrary malicious-code sandbox.
The finite controls verify declared supported discovery/identity/lifecycle behavior, not universal semantic test completeness or universal scanner correctness.
Canonical registration, portable documentation composition, current-head CI, integration and final federation gates remain the root integrator’s separate obligations.
